contexts.text: Flight = the last time; also that of each man when he dies.
As man of himself is dead...
When from being dead, man is made spiritual. Treated of. AC 81.
A dead man does not acknowledge any truth and good except that which is of the body and the world; this he adores.
The ends of a dead man regard only the life of the body and of the world, nor does he know what eternal life is, and what the Lord, is; and if he does know he does not believe.
A dead man, when in combat, almost always yields; and when in no combat, evils and falsities have dominion with him, and he is a servant. His bonds are external ones...
A dead man has not even conscience; and many do not know what conscience is, still less perception.
On the resuscitation of man from the dead. General article. HH 449. SE 300. SE 1092. SE 1115.

I was brought into a state of insensibility as to the bodily senses, thus almost into the state of the dying... so that I might perceive... the things which happen to those who have died, and are being resuscitated...
When the Angels perceive that their faces are received, they know that the man is dead.
They who are dying, for the most part think about eternal life, rarely about salvation and happiness; wherefore the Angels keep them in thought about eternal life.
Lest ye die ()... The reason why they would thus die, is that faith would thus perish, that is, all wisdom and intelligence.

The reason dead men rarely feel such misery and anxiety, is that they are no longer men, although they suppose themselves to be men more than others; for they do not know what the Spiritual and Celestial are, and what eternal life, any more than the brutes; and like them they look downwards to earthly things... They favour only the proprium, and indulge their genius and senses, with the consent of the whole Rational; and, being dead, they do not endure any combat or temptation; for, if it were to supervene, it would be more grievous than they could stand (vivere), and thus they would curse themselves still more, and would precipitate themselves still more deeply into infernal damnation; wherefore they are spared until they have passed into the other life, where they cannot any longer die from any temptation or misery; they then endure most grievous things. Signified.
The Lord's life with such a one is perverted, and becomes the life of evil, which is death; hence he is called dead.

On the other hand, they who are not in faith are called dead... as in Isaiah: The dead shall not live; the Rephaim shall not rise again, to this, that thou hast visited and extinguished them (); for those who are swollen with self-love... And Hell is called death, . They are also called the dead by the Lord, ; .
The man who is dead is not called dead because he will die after the life of the body, but because he will live the life of death; for death is damnation and Hell.
And he died () = that there was not such perception. AC 494, Explained.
The word die = everything that ceases to be such as it has been. Illustrated.

He who is destitute (of goods and truths) has not life, but is dead; the foods on which his soul is pastured when he is dead are delights from evils and pleasantnesses from falsities, which are the foods of death; also from corporeal, worldly, and natural things, which have nothing of life in them.
He that toucheth the dead shall be unclean seven days ()... in the internal sense = what is proper to man, which is dead and profane.
Hence it is that some... believe that when the body dies they will entirely die: but when they die, they then first begin to live.
Immediately after death they are elevated into Heaven...
After death they can meet all whom they have Known in the world, and of whom they have heard...
When his body dies, his soul lives.
Humiliation consists in the acknowledgement of self, that with self there is nothing alive, and nothing good, but that with self all is dead, nay, cadaverous.
With such, whose worship is called Babel, there does not exist internal worship, but there is a certain dead, in fact cadaverous thing interiorly, which is worshipped.
Haran died () = that interior worship was obliterated.
The Angels never have any idea of death, but only an idea of life.

As soon as he recedes from corporeal things, those which are of the soul and of life open, which also is the reason, not only that corporeal things must die before man can be born anew or regenerated, but also that the body must die, in order that he may come into Heaven, and see heavenly things. This is the case with the Word of the Lord; its corporeal things are those which are of the sense of the letter, and when the mind is kept in these things, internal ones are never seen, but when they have as it were died, they are first presented to view...
The Most Ancient Church regarded all earthly and worldly and also corporeal things... no otherwise than as dead things; but (by regarding them as representative) dead things lived with them.
The Angels said... that what is of stone, mortar, and wood, to them is dead; but that which is from the Lord, and from life and light itself, is alive...
The dead (; ) do not mean the dead, but the damned.
They do not believe that the dead will rise again until that time...
It is the Last Judgment to everyone immediately when he dies; for he then passes into the other life... and is judged either to death or to life... AC 4527:2. AC 4663.
No death, or transition to his fathers by death, is here signified.

They who die and are buried, do not die, but pass from a dim life to a clear one; for the death of the body is only the continuation, and also the perfection, of life; and then for the first time they who are of the Lord come into the enjoyment of all goods, which enjoyment is signified by a good old age.
(Preface.) [3]. It has been granted me... to speak there... with almost all those whom I have known in the life of the body and have died.
In the internal sense, death such as that of the body, is never perceived... for in the other life they are ignorant what death is.
To make the just die with the impious () = that what is good cannot die, because evil can be separated therefrom. Explained.
All little children who die... SE 3542.
Formerly, when they saw an Angel of Jehovah, they believed they were about to die. References, Explained.
Lest, perchance, some evil cleave to me, and I die () = that then it could not be otherwise than that he would be in evil, and thus would be damned.
Behold, thou shalt die on account of the woman () = that the doctrine of faith would become none, if the Rational were to be consulted as to the things which are there.
Know that dying thou shalt die () = that there would be no doctrine of truth and good.
Lest I see the death of the child () = grief because thus it would perish. To see death = to perish.
They who are being desolated as to goods and truths... in the privation of good and truth do not regard the death of the body, which they do not care for, but eternal death. Treated of.
Provided they will think... in the last hour of death... AC 3938:6. AC 4171:3.
To slay his son = even until whatever is from what is merely human is dead.
Hence it is that they are called dead men...

Sarah died () = night as to the truths of faith. To die, the dead, and death, when predicated of the Church, = its last time, when all faith, that is, charity, has expired; which time is called in the Word night. It is to die because it ceases to be such.
From upon the faces of the dead () = in that night.
In the opposite sense, sepulchre = death, or Hell.
He then dies as to the former man, and rises again as to the new one: through regeneration, man, from dead, becomes alive.

I will bury my dead from before me () = that thus he would emerge and rise again from the night which was with them... The dead = a state of shade or night, that is, of ignorance. AC 2923. AC 2925. AC 2931. AC 2948. AC 2961.
The dead = night as to the goods and truths of faith.
Human life is nothing but a progression from the world to Heaven; and the last, which is death, is the passage itself.
Abraham expired and died () = the end of the representation by Abraham. To expire and die = to cease, or have an end; here, the end of the representation. Explained. AC 3259. AC 3276.
The representatives in the Word are continuous, although they appear to be interrupted by the deaths of those who represented; whereas their deaths do not signify any interruption, but continuation.

Man cannot think spiritually immediately after death, except from those things which are of his Natural: the communication which man has while he lives in the body is exterior, but this ceases by the death of the body.

Esau said, Behold, I am going to die () = that he would afterwards rise again... To die = the last of a state, when anything ceases to be. References. And as the end of a former state is the beginning of the following one, here, by going to die, is signified to rise again afterwards.
They who dwell in the shadow of death () = the state of those who are in ignorance of good and truth.

He that toucheth this man and his woman, dying he shall die () = that Divine truth and Divine good is not to be opened, and is even not to be approached in faith, on peril of eternal damnation, if it is profaned... Dying to die = eternal damnation, which is spiritual death.

I do not know the day of my death () = life in the Natural... Death = to rise again, that is, to be resuscitated into life; thus by the day of death is signified the state of the resuscitation of life, or, what is the same, life. The reason it is in the Natural, is that life there is here treated of.
Before I die () = the first state of resuscitation in the Natural. To die = to rise again or be resuscitated into life. AC 3515. AC 3523.
That the Word... vivifies the dead, was represented by the man living again... who touched the bones of Elisha.
In the opposite sense, flesh = the voluntary proprium of man, which in itself is nothing but evil, and because not vivified by the Lord it is called dead, and hence this man is called dead.

Hence everyone can judge... that the truths of faith without the good of charity are dead... The reason truths still appear to be animated, although there is not the good of charity, is from the affections of the love of self and of the world, which have no other life than that which in the spiritual sense is called death, and is infernal life.
The breathing of Heaven... flows in by a wonderful correspondence into man's breathing, which is... of the body; and if man were deprived of this influx, he would fall down dead in a moment.
When the Church is devoid of the good and thence of the truth of faith... it is said to be dead... Hence, when dead, it is compared to a carcase.

And if not, I am dead () = that thus it would not rise again. To die = not to rise again into life. In ancient times, wives called themselves dead, when they did not bear a son or daughter, and also believed themselves to be such...
He who has not these births, namely, the truths of faith and the goods of charity, is as it were dead; that is, is among the dead who do not rise again, to wit, to life or Heaven.
When from a dead man he is becoming a living one; that is, from a corporeal a celestial one, he is led through many states...
Such a ritual was accepted when the wife was barren, lest she should represent the dead who do not rise again to life.
So long as natural affection is dominant, the man is called dead...
Unless works correspond to the good of faith... they are dead works, in which there is no good, nor truth.
Hence they could know that the state after death is much more clear and bright than the state before death; and that when a man dies, he passes comparatively from shade to light...
The life which a man has acquired in the world follows him, that is, he is in such life after death; for... no one can put off the life acquired from infancy, unless he were to die altogether...
The interior man is as it were dead as to good and truth, if the exterior or natural man does not correspond to him as to goods and truths.
If the Societies of Spirits and Angels in which man is were taken away... that moment he would fall down quite dead.
Wherefore, the man who is regenerate comes into a like thought (to that of the Angels) when he dies...
Hence... it was forbidden to eat that which had died of itself...
The privation (of spiritual and celestial love) is what is called spiritual death.
But this life is not life, but is, as it is called, spiritual death.
There is no spiritual confidence, except that which flows in through the good of love and of charity... thus not at the point of death.
He who can be conjoined with the Divine cannot die to eternity.
They do not know that the good will of the internal man remains after death, and that the works of the external man separated from him are dead, and perish.
It was granted to reply, that the life of the evil does indeed appear to them as life, but still it is the life which is called spiritual death...
So that they may be called effigies of death.
The man himself does not perceive this inundation while he lives in the body, but he comes into it after death...

Unless a man is in Heaven as to the thoughts and affections... he cannot come thither after death; for there is nothing of communication... for after death his mind cannot be opened towards the interiors...
This sphere, the man who has carried on such a life bears with him after death.
They who are able to be thus conjoined with the Divine do not die when the corporeal things which are of the world are separated; for the interiors remain conjoined.
When a man dies (they say he is happy, etc.). AC 5078:5.
Deborah the nurse of Rebekah died () = that hereditary evil was expelled. To die = an end, or to cease to be such; here, therefore, expelled, because it treats of hereditary evil.
Hence it was customary to weep for the dead when they were being buried.
As the tree falls so it lies, or as a man dies so he becomes... AC 6368:end, Explained.

In the going forth of her soul that she was about to die () = a state of temptations. The going forth of the soul, and to die = the last of temptation, which is when the old man dies and the new one receives life.
Rachel died, and was buried in the way of Ephrath () = the end of the former affection of interior truth. To die = to cease to be such. AC 6243.

Isaac expired and died () = exsuscitation in the Divine Natural. To expire and die = exsuscitation. References. For when it is mentioned in the Word of anyone that he is dead, in the internal sense is signified the last of him and what is new in another, thus continuation: as when it is related of the kings of Judah and Israel that they are dead, or of the chief priests, in the internal sense it is the end of the representation by them, and the continuation in another, thus exsuscitation. They, too, who are in the other life, and are with man while he is reading these things, do not apprehend any death, because they are utterly ignorant of what it is to die; hence, in place thereof they perceive what is continuous in another. Moreover, when a man dies, he does not die, except as to the Corporeal which has served him for uses on earth; but he continues life as to his spirit in the World where corporeal things are no longer of any use.
For, when the body is dead, the soul rises again.
Hence all things which are of death in the natural world, signify such things as are of life in the Spiritual World.

With the Sensitive of man immediately after death, the case is this. As soon as a man dies, and the corporeal things with him grow cold, he is exsuscitated into life, and is then in the state of all sensations, so much so, that at first he scarcely knows otherwise than that he is still in the body. The sensations in which he is, lead him to believe so; but when he perceives that he has more exquisite sensations, and this especially when he begins to speak with other Spirits, he notices that he is in the other life, and that the death of his body has been the continuation of the life of his spirit. Example(s).

Hence many... know no otherwise, than that all sense is in the organs of the body, and therefore when these organs fall to pieces by death, they suppose that no sense survives; when yet the man, that is, his spirit, then comes into his veriest sensitive life.
(Aristotle) said, that he knew his spirit would live after death, because it was his interior essence, which cannot die, because it can think...
They who are in Heaven are brought by the Lord into a more perfect life, and at last even into the flower of their youth; so, also, they who have died in a good old age.
Under Body, see these references. AC 5078:3.

Still, this influx manifests itself by this, that most are solicitous about their burial and about encomiums after death... for without this influx, they would have utterly despised all memory of themselves after they had died.
They conspired against (Joseph) to make him die () = that they wanted to extinguish the Divine Spiritual which is from the Lord's Divine Human... To make to die = to extinguish.
(How the proposition that man lives after death may be confirmed both negatively and affirmatively.)
When the Divine truth will appear in its own light, as takes place with every man when he dies. Signified.

Jehovah made (Er) die () = that there was no representative of the Church. To die = to cease to be such; also the end of the representation; here, therefore, that there was no representative of the Church with any posterity from him.
Lest perchance (Shelah) die also, as his brothers () = fear lest he should perish, namely, the representative of the Church which was with the posterity from Jacob.

The daughter of Shuah died () = as to evil from falsity. To die = to cease to be such... Here, therefore, by the daughter of Shuah died after many days, is signified a change of state as to evil from falsity, that it was not such as it had been before.
His own life, without difference, remains with everyone after death.
When man comes into the other life, which takes place immediately after death...

Man's life in the world is scarcely as a moment relatively to his life after death; but there are few who believe that they will live after death... But this I can assert, that man is in the other life immediately after death, and that there his life in the world is just continued...
This pleasure is dead, because it is from Hell.

They who are in evil appear, especially to themselves, as if they have life, but it is such life as in the Word is called death, and it also is spiritual death; for they taste nothing of good, and understand nothing of truth...
Hence it is that men after death mutually see each other, and are in society together according to the interiors...

These things, namely, the exterior things of the Natural, man leaves behind when he dies; but the former ones, namely, the interior things of the Natural, he takes with him into the other life, where they serve as a plane to spiritual and celestial things. For man, when he dies, loses nothing, except the bones and the flesh...
Man, when he dies, has all the Natural with him; and such as it has been formed with him in the world, such it also remains...

As with man there is a connection with the Divine, and his inmost is such that it can receive the Divine, and not only receive it, but also appropriate it to himself through acknowledgement and affection, thus through what is reciprocal; therefore man, because he is thus implanted with the Divine, can never die...

Many of the learned believe that life is in the body, and thus that when the body dies they will also die as to the interiors on account of the coherence; when yet it is only the exterior degree which dies...
When man dies, and enters into the other life, his life is circumstanced as is the food, which is softly received by the lips...

That we may live, and not die () = spiritual life... In the other life... by death is signified in general Hell, and in special eternal unhappiness there... and as in Hell there is... evil in place of good and falsity in place of truth, and thus spiritual life is extinguished, therefore relatively there is death there; for spiritual death is evil and falsity; and with man it is to will evil and thence to think falsity. Evil Genii and Spirits do not want to hear that it is said of them that they do not live, or that they are dead; for they say that they have life because they are able to will and to think; but it is said to them, that as there is life in good and truth, there cannot possibly be in evil and falsity, for they are contrary.
Ye shall not die () = that thus there is life in truths.
Because his brother is dead () = as the Internal is not present... To be dead, here, = not to be present; for he was among the living, but was not present.

We will arise, and go, and live, and not die () = spiritual life according to degrees... Not to die = to be damned no longer, but to be outside of a state of damnation; for in the internal sense of the Word no other death is meant than spiritual death which is damnation. Hence it is evident that... removal from those things which are not of life is signified by not to die.
For all things in the Natural of themselves are dead, but are vivified by influx from the Spiritual World...
That man has death from evils, or on account of sin, is known in the Church; thus, also, he has diseases, for these are of death. AC 5726, Explained.
With whomsoever of thy servants it be found, let him die () = that he is damned who does such a thing. To die = to be damned; for spiritual death is nothing else but damnation.
And his brother is dead () = that there is no internal good... To be dead = to be no longer.
If he should leave his father, he would die () = that if it were separated the Church would perish... To die = to be no longer, thus to perish. AC 5836.
If confidence appears with the evil when... death is at the doors, that confidence is spurious or false...

This is circumstanced as is death and the things of death. In the spiritual sense, these do not signify natural death, but spiritual death, which is damnation; for there is no other death in the Spiritual World.

The two Spirits who are adjoined to man, cause that there is communication with Hell, and the two Angels cause that there is communication with Heaven... If these communications were taken away, man would fall down as dead as a stock; for there would then be taken away the connection with the First Being... From experience.

I will go and see him before I die () = a longing for conjunction before there is what is new... Before I die = before what is new, namely, what is new of representation; for in the Word representatives so succeed each other, that when one dies, there follows a representative either similar by means of some one else, or another one, thus what is new; as when Abraham died, there succeeded the representative by Isaac; and when he died, there succeeded the representative by Jacob; and when he died, there succeeded the representative by his descendants. AC 6302:2.
The death which wastes in noon-day () = the evil which is openly lived, by which truth is destroyed. AC 7102:10. AC 8505. AC 9642:5.

To place the hand upon the eyes means that the external Sensuous, or that of the body, is closed, and the internal Sensuous opened... This takes place when they die, because by death is signified resuscitation into life; for when man dies, he does not die; but only lays down the body which had served him for use in the world, and passes into the other life in a body which serves him for use there.

This time let me die () = new life. To die = resurrection into life, thus new life. The reason to die = what is new of life... is that when man dies, what is new of his life at once begins; he is exsuscitated into life when the material body is rejected which had served him for use in the world. New life is here signified by to die, because this comes by virtue of influx from the Internal...

This is especially evident from the state of man after death; he is then able to think and speak rationally about the truths and goods of faith, and this much more perspicaciously than in the life of the body, but he cannot take any scientifics out of the memory...
Why should we die near thee because the silver faileth? () = that otherwise there is spiritual death on account of the lack of truth. To die = spiritual death... or damnation. Explained, Illustrated.

Wherefore shall we die at thine eyes, both we and our ground? () = that if they were desolated there would no longer be spiritual life under the Internal... These receptacles (of spiritual life) are said to die, when inwardly there is not anything of spiritual life; for by to die is signified desolation; that is, the privation of good and truth, which make spiritual life.

That we may live, and not die () = spiritual life thence, and no longer the fear of damnation... To die = damnation; here, the fear of damnation; because, in a state of desolation, when man is being regenerated, there is not damnation, but the fear of damnation.

And the time drew near for Israel to die () = the state just before regeneration... To die = to rise again, and to be excited into spiritual life, thus to be regenerated; for he who is being regenerated, rises again from spiritual death, and is excited into new life. AC 6221.

That to die = regeneration, and that to be sick = what is successive of regeneration, must appear far-fetched. (But) the Angels know nothing about death, nor about sickness, wherefore they have no idea about them, and therefore, in their place, when this is being read by man, they have the idea of continuation of life and resurrection; for this reason, that when man dies, he only puts off that which had served him for use in the world, and enters into the life in which he had been with his spirit: this idea comes to the Angels when dying and sickness are being read of: in like manner the idea of regeneration, for this is resurrection into life; as before man was spiritually dead; but when he is regenerated he becomes alive, and a son of the resurrection. The man himself, who while he lives in the body, longs for Heaven, thinks no otherwise about death and the sickness which precedes it, than that it is resurrection into life; for when he is thinking about Heaven, he abstracts himself from an idea about the body, especially when he is sick and comes near to death. Hence it is evident, that a spiritual idea about the death of the body is that of what is new of life...
When to redeem is predicated of death, those are meant who are in damnation.

Israel said to Joseph, Behold, I die () = the perception of spiritual good from the Celestial Internal concerning new life, and concerning the end of the representation... To die = resuscitation into life; and also the end of the former representation... References.
The third part of the creatures that are in the sea, that had souls, died ()... That they died = that they had not spiritual life.
To expire, or die = new life. References.
He who conceives exterior and interior things as continually purer, and thus coherent by continuity... cannot apprehend otherwise, than that when the external dies the internal dies too...
The reason this Church is described by Israel now dead... is that in the internal sense by death is not signified death... but new life; and by burial, regeneration. References.
Behold, I die () = that the Church ceased to be. To die = no longer to be; and also the last time of the Church, when it expires. References.

And Joseph's brethren saw that their father was dead () = things alienated from truth and good, and the apperception that the Church is to be exsuscitated... To be dead = to be resuscitated, namely, the Church. References.
Thy father commanded before he died () = that it was by command of the Church... Before he died = while the Church still was.

And Joseph said to his brethren, Behold, I die () = a prediction that the Internal of the Church would cease... To die = to cease to be such, thus to cease. To die, also, = the last time of the Church. References.
And Joseph died () = that the Internal of the Church ceased to be.

Joseph was dead () = when the Internal of the Church was now circumstanced otherwise. To die = the end of the former state, and the beginning of a new one, thus that the state of the Church was now circumstanced otherwise. That to die = to cease to be such. References. And that it = the end of the former representation. References.
The state of the Church, such as it is now, is described in what follows; also its external states, which is signified by his brethren being dead, and all that generation.
In subjects which disagree with good, there is presented a life contrary to spiritual life, which in the Word is called death.
For he who takes away faith, takes away spiritual life; the life which remains is the life which is called death.
And the king of Egypt died () = the end of the former falsity. To die = to cease to be, thus the end.
All the men are dead that seek thy soul () = the removal of the falsities which endeavour to destroy the life of truth and good. To be dead = to be removed; for they who are dead are also removed.
For there adheres to man, and is in his memories, after death, everything of his thought in the world, of intention, of will, of speech, and of his action...
As to die, in the spiritual sense, is not to die, but to be deprived of truth and good, and to be in falsity and evil, and therefore to be damned.

Therefore when they suppose themselves to be deprived of the truths and goods of faith and charity, they are affected with an agony like those who are in the death agony, for they see spiritual death before them, that is, damnation.
The fish that is in the river shall die () = that scientific truth will be extinguished... To die = to be extinguished.
The frogs died out of the houses, etc () = that with them there ceased reasonings from mere falsities everywhere in the Natural. To die = to cease.
This contrary of life is Hell, and is called death; and they are called the dead. Illustrated.
There shall nothing die of all that is the Sons of Israel's () = that they shall not be consumed. Explained.

That which is conjoined with life itself and what is eternal cannot die, that is, be consumed; it remains to eternity, and is continually being perfected. But those things which are of faith with those who are of the Church and are being damned, as they are not conjoined with the Divine, and thence have no life in themselves, do die... In the other life they are consumed, that is, taken away.

The hail shall descend upon them, and they shall die () = that what is of the Church will be entirely destroyed by falsity... To die = to cease to be; and as it is said of the vastation of good and truth, it = to be destroyed.
That he may remove from upon me this death only () = that this falsity may not torment... For by death is signified damnation and Hell, thus also torment.
For in the day thou seest my faces thou shalt die () = if it should enter into the animus, it would be extirpated... To die = to be extirpated.
By the death (of the first-born) is signified the damnation itself.
For there was no house where there was not one dead () = because there was none not damned.
We all die () = Hell with them. To die = Hell. References.

The inhabitants of Jupiter said to me, that they do not fear death, except a little on account of the loss of their married partner and children; because they know for certain that the death of the body is the continuation of life, and that they afterwards become more happy. AC 8850.

Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us to die in the wilderness? () = that if there were damnation, it would be all the same whether it came through the falsities of the infesters, or through a state of temptations in which they yielded... Graves = damnation... To die also = damnation.

It would be better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness () = that damnation through the violence of falsity in a state of infestations would be preferable to the damnation consequent upon yielding in a state of temptations. Explained.
Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the sea-shore () = the aspect of the damned dispersed here and there. Explained.
At the presence of the Divine, the evil... conduct themselves as do those who are in the agony of death...
These (evils) bring the spiritual life to the death which is called spiritual death, and is damnation, as diseases bring the natural life to its death.
Repentance... in a compulsory state avails not; a compulsory state is... a state of imminent death, etc.

To have died by the hand of Jehovah () = that they are left by the Lord. To be dead = to be in evils and consequent falsities, thus in damnation; and when it is said to die by the hand of Jehovah, it = to be left by the Lord; for they who are left by Him, that is, who leave Him, rush into evils and consequent falsities, and thus into damnation.
Flesh = what is dead; spirit, what is alive... Dead is said of what is evil; for from evil comes spiritual death...
If they do not repent, death is denounced against them.
To make me to die, and my sons, and my cattle, of thirst () = that from the lack of truth, everything of spiritual life would expire. To die = to expire; here, as to the spiritual life.
Everyone that toucheth the mount, dying he shall die () = that the man of the Spiritual Church who infuses himself even to the celestial will perish.
Those (of the inhabitants of Jupiter) see such (a bald head) as will die within a year.

Wherefore, they do not call dying dying, but being heaven-made. Those in that Earth who have lived happy in marriage love... do not die by diseases, but tranquilly as in sleep, and thus transmigrate out of the world into Heaven.
(Why they die so young in Jupiter.)
Man is such as is his will, and such he remains after death; because death is not the end of life, but its continuation. AC 8939. LJCont 32.
Lest we die () = that thus the life of Heaven will perish with them. To die = to die spiritually, thus to perish as to the life of Heaven.

I can assert that man, as soon as he dies, is in the other life, and lives a Spirit among Spirits; and that he then appears to himself and all others precisely as a man in the world, endowed with every sense, both internal and external; thus that the death of the body is only the casting away of such things as had served for use and function in the world; and, moreover, that death itself is a continuation of life, but in another World... I speak yet and have spoken with almost all whom I have known in the world, and are dead; with some, after two or three days from death. Most of them are highly indignant that they had not believed that any life would remain after death...
That which is from Own intelligence is in itself devoid of life, nay, spiritually is dead...
(The Spirits of Saturn) then say that they want to die... When asked why they do so, they say that they would rather die, than be withdrawn from the Lord. SE 1517.

In the other life they can never be brought to a state of good, that is, so as to act from good; for the life remains with everyone after death: such as a man is when he dies, such he remains... Not such as he is about the hour of death; but such as he is when he dies from the whole course of his life...
He that smiteth a man and he dies () = injury of the truth of faith, and the consequent loss of spiritual life... To die = the loss of spiritual life.

Dying he shall die () = damnation... The reason death = damnation, is that with those who are damned the truths of faith and the goods of love are extinguished; for these are what constitute the veriest life of man... When these are extinguished, falsities and evils succeed in their place, which, being opposite... are of death; but of spiritual death, which is damnation, Hell, eternal unhappiness...
Thou shalt take him from Mine altar to die () = damnation even if he flees to the worship of the Lord, and supplicates for forgiveness, and promises repentance.
Dying he shall die = damnation. AC 9020. AC 9022. AC 9191.
And he die not () = and is not extinguished. To die = to cease to be such, thus to be extinguished.
And he die under his hand () = so that it be extinguished under his view.
And he die () = even so as to destroy it.
And his lord also shall die () = the damnation of the internal man.
The natural life without the spiritual life is dead.

And the dead one shall be his () = that evil or falsity will remain with him. AE 537:7... The dead one, when said concerning good or truth in the Natural, which is signified by an ox or a donkey, = evil or falsity; for when good dies evil succeeds (in its place), and when truth dies falsity succeeds. As what is dead = evil and falsity, those are called the dead who will evil and believe falsity.
And he die () = so that the good affection perishes. To die = to perish.

They shall also divide the dead one () = also the affection that does the injury. The dead one = evil and falsity; hence by the dead ox is signified the affection of evil and falsity in the Natural, thus the affection that does the injury; for evil injures through falsity.
1.2. And the dead one shall be his () = for the affection that does the injury..., The dead one = evil and falsity.
To die = to be extinguished. AC 9175.
To die = extinction and loss.
When a man dies the external breathing ceases, but the internal breathing... remains...
The dead () = those who, from ignorance of the truth of faith, as yet have not spiritual life.
When the truths of faith and the goods of love are falsified and perverted, the man is sick; but when they are denied at heart, the man spiritually dies.
He hath filled with carcases = thus spiritual death, which is the total deprivation of truth and good.
That he die not () = lest the representative perish, and thus conjunction with the Heavens.
Lest they bear their iniquity and die () = the annihilation of all worship... for representative worship died...
All things from the sun of the world are dead.
By the Sensuous which is the ultimate of the Natural, is properly meant that which is called flesh, and perishes when man dies. (See Sensuous at this and other references.)
For such as is the Natural of man when he dies, such it remains... for it is the plane into which interior things flow...

That they die not () = that the representative perish not. To die, when said of the ministration of Aaron and his sons, = the cessation of the representatives, and thence of conjunction with Heaven. Explained.
All goods and truths... without life from the Lord in them, are dead things; nay, are even evil ones...
To die () = to perish as to the spiritual life.

Dying he shall die () = separation from Heaven and spiritual death. To die, when said in relation to the Sabbath, by which is signified the Lord and the acknowledgement of Him, = no conjunction with Heaven, thus separation from it; and separation from Heaven is spiritual death.

If anyone (in the Third Earth) thinks and does evil, he is reproved by a certain Spirit, who denounces death against him, if he persists therein; and, moreover, if he does persist he dies by a swoon. SE 1682.
Man has been so created, that as to his Internal he cannot die... NJHD 224.
The death (of those who died in the plague) () = the extinction of all truths. This takes place with those who profane.
Everyone that doeth work in it shall die () = spiritual death with those who are led by themselves and their own loves, and not by the Lord... To die = damnation, or spiritual death.
Wherefore, their life is not called life, but spiritual death.
They wanted me to tell them that they are not dead...
Little children who die...
The nature of the difference between those who die as little children, and those who die as adults...
Some Societies of Angels are present with those who are being exsuscitated from the dead.

When the body is separated from its spirit, it is said to die: the man still remains a man, and lives. I have heard from Heaven, that some who die, while they lie on the bier, before they are resuscitated, think in their cold body...
On the resuscitation of man from the dead. General article.

When the body can no longer perform its functions... man is said to die. This takes place when the respiratory motions of the lungs and the systolic ones of the heart cease. But still, the man does not die; but is only separated from the Corporeal which had been of use to him in the world... Hence it is evident, that man, when he dies, only passes from one world into the other. Hence it is, that in the Word, in the internal sense, death = resurrection, and the continuation of life, HH 445. [Swedenborg footnote 1.], References.
That man after death is in all the sense, memory, thought, affection, in which he is in the world; and that he leaves nothing behind except his earthly body. General article.

[Swedenborg footnote 1.] As man's understanding can receive faith in God, and his will love to God, man can be conjoined with God in faith and love, and he who can be conjoined with God in love and faith, cannot die to eternity. References.
This appearing of life is what is called spiritual death.
On the first state of man after death. General article.
Some do not undergo these states; but immediately after death are either carried into Heaven, or cast into Hell... I have seen some carried up an hour after death.
Thus is the one life continued into the other, and death is only the passage.
At last they drew their breath as if they were moribund, or dying.
For this reason they also call death only a translation from one world into another like one.
The natural man is he who is called dead.
The confidence of faith separated is dead.
Dead men, that is, they who are not in faith and love to God and in love towards the neighbour, are not admitted into temptations, because they would yield. References.
When man passes from the natural world into the Spiritual, which takes place when he dies...
About the time of death, when they are no longer in worldly and corporeal things, they believe that they will come into Heaven (at once).
The state of man cannot be changed after death.
That which can be thus conjoined with the Divine, cannot die to eternity; for the Divine is with him and conjoins him to Itself.

Every man after death lives to eternity; therefore no Angel or Spirit ever thinks about death, nay, they do not know at all what it is to die; wherefore, when death is mentioned in the Word, there is understood by the Angels either damnation, which is death in the spiritual sense, or the continuation of life and resurrection.
[Swedenborg's footnote]. When death is mentioned in the Word, where the evil are treated of, in Heaven there is understood damnation, which is spiritual death; also Hell. References.
[Swedenborg's footnote]. They who are in evils and falsities are called dead. References.

[Swedenborg's footnote]. By death, where it treats of the good who die, in Heaven is understood resurrection and continuation of life; because then man rises again, continues his life, and enters upon the eternal one. References.
Hence it is evident, that death is only the continuation of life, and that it is only a passage.
Death () = eternal damnation.
That the dead were resuscitated (by the Lord) = that those became alive who would otherwise have spiritually perished.
Fire is dead, and the solar fire is death itself...
When a man dies...
The sun of the natural world is pure fire, and thence dead; and nature, because it derives origin from that sun, is dead. General article. AE 1207:2.
What is dead does nothing whatever of itself...

Therefore the heat proceeding from it is dead, and likewise the light... is dead. The atmospheres, too, which receive the heat and light of that sun, are dead. Since these are dead, all things... which are under the atmospheres... are dead. TCR 75:2.
It follows, that nature... is dead. TCR 77:3.
(It follows) that spaces also may be called dead.
All these states (of the day and year), because they are not states of life, as in the Spiritual World, are also dead.
A person thus becomes sensuous natural, a spiritually dead man.
Without two suns, the one living and the other dead, there can be no creation. General article.
As all natural things from their origin are dead... it follows that the other sun is dead; also, that the dead sun itself is created through the living sun...
A dead sun was created for this reason...

That nothing (was created) through the dead sun, (for) what is living disposes what is dead... For what is dead to act upon what is living, or a dead force upon a living force, or, what is the same, what is natural upon what is spiritual, is entirely contrary to order... What is dead, or what is natural, may indeed be perverted or changed in many ways by external accidents, but still it cannot act upon life...
There is nothing so inert and dead as to be totally devoid of working power...
When man puts off the natural degree, which is the case when he dies...
Still, the man with whom the spiritual degree has been opened, comes into this wisdom when he dies.

These (natural) substances recede when man dies, but not the spiritual substances (of the natural mind); wherefore, the same mind after death... remains in a form similar to that which it had in the world.
The substances of the natural world are in themselves dead... and those substances which are dead... from their nature resist, and so from their nature react.
So the man, from being alive, becomes dead. He is said to be... dead, whose mind is a Hell.

When the correspondence of (the cardiac and pulmonary) motions ceases, a separation takes place, which is death. Separation or death takes place, when, from any disease or accident, the body comes into such a state, that it cannot act as one with its spirit... DWis 7. 4.

Evil and falsity together are not anything, because there is nothing of spiritual life in them; which is the reason why the life of the infernals is not called life, but death; therefore, as everything is of life, there cannot be any thing of death.
a. Speech with the dead...
It is of the Divine Providence that man puts off natural and temporary things by death. General article.
This is effected through the rejection of the temporary and natural ultimates, which is the death of the body.
The necessaries of life; food, clothing, and habitation... are also put off and left behind by death...

a. So, too, does man's life, when he dies, remain such as it has been... For death is a continuation of life, with the difference, that man cannot then be reformed... For the ultimates of life that man carries with him after death, become quiescent...
Wherefore the natural man, however civilly and morally he may act, is called dead.

The mortal in man is his material body, which is taken away by its death. That man's mind cannot die, was seen by the sages... for they said, How can the mind die, when it is able to be wise? Explained.
But yet as they were born men, and are thereby in the faculty of thinking and willing, and thence in the faculty of speaking and acting, they cannot die...
I fell at His feet as dead () = a failing of his Own life. AE 78.
And was dead () = that He has been neglected, and His Divine Human not acknowledged. AR 93.
I have the keys of Hell and of death () = that He alone can save. AE 86.

Be thou faithful unto death () = the reception and acknowledgement of Truths, even until falsities are removed, and as it were abolished... With those in the Spiritual World there is no death, wherefore by death here, is meant the end of their temptations.

Shall not be hurt by the second death () = that afterwards they will not yield to evils and falsities from Hell. By the first death is meant the death of the body, and by the second death is meant the death of the soul, which is damnation. AR 525:end. AE 128.
I will kill her sons with death () = that all the truths from the Word with them will be turned into falsities... To kill her sons with death, also = to damn their falsities.
Thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead () = that it seems and is believed by themselves and others, that they are spiritually alive, when yet they are spiritually dead. AE 186.
Strengthen the things that are left, which are about to die () = that those things which are of their worship may receive life, and not be extinguished.

The name of him that sat on him was death () = the extinction of spiritual life... By death is here signified spiritual death, which is the extinction of spiritual life; and by Hell is signified damnation, which follows that death. Illustrated. AE 383.

(To kill) by death () = through the love of proprium... The reason that by death is signified the love of man's proprium, is that by death is signified the extinction of spiritual life, and thence natural life separated from spiritual life...
The pestilence, and death = plenary consumption, and thus damnation.
The third part of those creatures in the sea, and had souls, died () = that those who have lived and do live that faith cannot be reformed and receive life.
Many men died of the waters, because they were made bitter () = the extinction of spiritual life with a number from the falsified truths of the Word. AE 521.

In those days men shall seek death, and shall not find it, and shall desire to die, and death shall flee from them () = that those who are in the doctrine of faith separated want the understanding to be closed up and the will to be stopped up in the things of faith, and thus that they should not have any spiritual light and life; but that still it is provided by the Lord, that the understanding should not be closed up, nor the will stopped up, lest spiritual light and life should be extinguished with men... For by death no other death is meant than spiritual death, which is induced when the understanding is removed from the things which are to be believed... AE 550. AE 551.

The time of judging the dead () = the last judgment upon those who have not any spiritual life... By the dead who are to be judged, in the universal sense, are meant the dead from the world; but in the proper sense, those who have not any spiritual life. Illustrated. AE 694, Explained.

They loved not their soul even unto death () = those who have not loved themselves more than the Lord... Even unto death = to want rather to die; consequently, to love the Lord above all things, and the neighbour as themselves; and to want rather to die, than recede from these two loves.

Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from henceforth () = the state of those after death who will be of His New Church... By the dead are signified those who have afflicted their soul, crucified their flesh, and suffered temptations. Explained, Illustrated.

It became as the blood of one dead, and every living soul died in the sea () = infernal falsity with them, through all the truth of the Word... having been extinguished... For by death is signified the extinction of spiritual life, and thence by what is dead is signified what is infernal... AE 966.
Death () = infernal life and intestine grief from being cast down from dominion.
In the Word throughout, it is said that they are killed... nay, dead, (which means) that they have been rejected by those who are in evils and falsities.
The rest of the dead () = those who have been rejected by those who are in faith alone...

Upon these the second death hath no Power () = that they have not damnation. By the second death nothing else is signified than spiritual death, which is damnation; for the first death is natural death, which is the death of the body; but the second death is spiritual death, which is the death of the soul... And as the second death is damnation, and the first death is decease, and this death is not spiritual, the first death is nowhere mentioned in the Apocalypse... He who has not observed this may easily believe that there are two spiritual deaths, because it is said the second death; when yet there is only one spiritual death, which is here meant by the second death.
I saw the dead small and great standing before God () = all who are dead from the earth, and are now among those who are in the World of Spirits. AR 868.

By the dead in the Word is signified the same as by deaths, and by deaths are signified various things; for by death is not only signified the extinction of natural life, which is decease, but also the extinction of spiritual life, which is damnation. By death is also signified the extinction of the loves of the body or the concupiscences of the flesh... In like manner, by death is signified resurrection, because after death, man at once rises again. By death is also signified neglect, no acknowledgement, and rejection by the world. In the most general sense, by death is signified the same as by the devil, wherefore also the devil is called death... Hence, also, by death is meant evil of the will, which makes man a devil. In this sense is death used in the following verse, where it is said, that death and Hell gave up their dead.
The sea gave up the dead who were in it () = the external and natural men of the Church called to judgment.

And death and Hell gave up the dead who were in them () = the men of the Church impious at heart, who were in themselves devils and satans, called to judgment... Death = those who were interiorly devils; and Hell those who were interiorly satans...

And death and Hell were cast into the lake of fire () = that the impious at heart, who in themselves were devils and satans, and yet in externals were as men of the Church, were cast down into Hell...
This is the second death () = that these have damnation itself.
Death shall be no longer () = that the Lord will take away all fear of damnation.
That everything which proceeds from this sun, regarded in itself, is dead. General article.
These, on account of this inversion, are they who are called the dead. Illustrated.
They are called the dead, because spiritual death is damnation.
When, by death, the soul emigrates from the natural world into its spiritual one...
From this, man has spiritual death, which, regarded in itself, is natural life without spiritual.
It is known from the Word that faith without charity is dead; but I will tell whence comes its death. Its death is from cold... first it dies as to its power to see...
On dead charity. General article.
Charity is dead with those with whom faith is dead. Explained.
What is natural... is a passive or a dead force.
(The power of evil Spirits to cause death).
About five months after his death...
Because they were not so long dead...
The Souls of the dead... SE 326. SE 333. SE 342.
The dead... can clearly and sensibly smell the quality of a subject that is dead...
That man in a state of integrity could never die.

1.2. There was shown me a dead head... which they see who are to die within a year, in order that they may prepare themselves for death, which they do not fear, except on account of leaving their friends... SE 743.
(In Jupiter) they die in their early manhood, to prevent too great an increase of men; but they rarely die through diseases... but they die tranquilly, and as in sleep.
Death is denounced against such, and for the most part is effected by the taking away of their breath... and rarely by diseases... They do not call it dying, but rather being Heaven-made.
The first state of one who is dying...
They then know that the man is dead.
When man dies, the celestial are at once present...
It matters nothing whether a man dies in his bed, or in battle, or in any other way...
The thoughts which a man entertains at the point of death...
That the quality of the ends of life may be evident... when death is imminent.
(His arrangements) at the point of death.
Not to want to die on account of the children is natural...
The evil also at the point of death can lightly esteem worldly things...
But they who care nothing for death, from the love of self...
In the dead these openings are closed.
Because in the hour of death he had thought of such a suction...
Whatever happens in the last hour of death, long remains.
When man dies...
They are effigies of death...
He then came into the Society of those who say that to die or live is all the same...
(I said) that in battles or dangers they ought not to fear to die...
He was behind, as it were dead...
It is forbidden them... to approach a dead man.
They had feared death for the sake of their life in the world...
In the anxiety of death they could be in a state of receiving...
(Situation of) those who have not feared death.
Death itself is from no other cause than sin. Explained.
This Corporeal belongs to man; this dies and becomes a corpse.
The interiors of man, which do not die. Enumerated.
When a man is about to die, he nods his head, and at last falls down. See SE 4686:end.
The reasons why boys, young men, adults, old people die. Enumerated.
When once they come to a man, they do not leave him until death.
If they come to men, they at once inflict death on them...
If anyone describes the state of one dying or dead...
The Angels said that in the houses (in that neighbourhood of Stockholm) there was not anyone alive, but all were dead, spiritually...
Asked whether they knew an example of those who had lived evilly, and had received their faith in the hours about death, and had repented...
On the resuscitation of the dead.
If they are not driven away, they induce death on man...
Polhem died on the Monday, and spoke with me on the Thursday...
Hence He is called the Firstborn of the dead...
Spirits cannot die; wherefore, if they are evil, at the Divine presence they die with spiritual death.
Spiritual death is turning away and removal from the Lord... This turning away and removal is what is called spiritual death; the Spiritual of Heaven is also dead with them.
And was dead = rejected; for the Lord is said to be dead when there is no faith and love to Him... With these, it is said that the Lord is dead, because He is rejected. AE 114.
Be thou faithful unto death = permanence in truths to the end.
Shall not be hurt by the second death = shall come into the New Heaven.
The second death is damnation; hence, to be hurt by it is to be damned...
I will kill her sons with death = that thus falsities are extinguished.
Dying he shall die () = to perish with eternal death, which is damnation.
As death = damnation, it also = Hell. Illustrated. AE 186:6. AE 186:8.
Hence it is evident that dead = those who have not the life of Heaven in them, consequently, who are in evils and thence falsities. Illustrated.
Strengthen the things... that are about to die = lest moral life perish by evils and falsities...
Hence it is that all things with him in themselves are dead, thus are about to die, unless vivified...
He that overcometh = him who perseveres even until death.
Evils which are known to be evils, and still enter, are meant by the death which wastes at noonday.
Everyone that liveth and believeth in Me, shall not die to eternity ()... Not to die = not to die spiritually, that is, to be damned; for the life of the damned is called death.
To snatch their soul from death () = from evils and falsities, and consequently from damnation.
He will swallow up death in eternity () = that the Lord by His Advent will remove evils and falsities with those who live from Him... Death = evil, because from it is spiritual death.
To die = to perish spiritually, or as to the life of Heaven. AE 521.
He is said to be dead, when he is not vivified from the spiritual man, that is, through influx out of Heaven from the Lord through the spiritual man...
Death is come up through the windows, it hath come into our palaces () = that infernal falsity has entered into the understanding, and thence into all things of thought and affection. AE 652:27.
There shall ye die () = thence is the desolation of the Church and damnation.
Wherefore, where the death of man is mentioned in the Word, instead of it the Angels perceive his transmigration from one world into the other.
A dead [body] () = one who has perished through evils.
Among the dead, neglected () = among those who have nothing of truth and good, and are therefore rejected.
Falsities from evil are signified by deaths (), since they who are in them are spiritually dead.
To die () = to perish.
To make a covenant with death () = conjunction by means of falsity from Hell, from which man spiritually dies.
That they will be taught and regenerated through truths from Him, is signified by thy dead shall live ().

They loved not their soul even unto death = the faithful who for the sake of these truths have suffered temptations, and have made nothing of the life of the world in comparison with the life of Heaven.
We are... among the living as the dead () = that they are able to be in spiritual life through the Word, and yet are not because they are in falsities.
Wounded to death () = to disagree with the Word; for the doctrine which disagrees with the Word is dead... AE 786.
Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from henceforth = the resurrection into eternal life of those who have lived the life of charity hitherto, and will live it henceforth.

The reason death = resurrection, and that therefore the dead = those who rise again to eternal life, is that death = Hell, and consequently evils and falsities; and these must die in order that man may receive spiritual life; for before these are dead and extinguished man has not spiritual life... wherefore, by dying here and elsewhere in the Word, is meant the extinction of man's Own life... Moreover, by dying in the spiritual sense may be meant resurrection... Natural death, too, is nothing but resurrection...
Hence it is evident, that death = both spiritual death, which is damnation, and also resurrection into life, which is salvation. Illustrated.
That natural death, which is the rejection of the unclean things of the body, and spiritual death, which is the removal of the unclean things of the spirit, signified resurrection. Illustrated.
The Lord's death and burial... means the purification of His Human, and glorification.
Death = when there is not anything good; for then man is spiritually dead.
Under Half-dead, see this reference.
The forces which are in nature from its origin... are dead forces. Explained.
It is said that the Lord has conquered death... for death = Hell, because all there are called dead.
With man, evil cannot be expelled, but is removed... therefore man dies as to the body.
(The Moravians) are not tolerated in any heavenly Society, because they think within themselves that all others but themselves are dead; thus the Angels would have a dead idea about themselves.
Diabolical love, which is death itself...
Their life appears... to the Angels as death.
4. 2. Man is not dead until the motion of the heart ceases. Explained.
3a. The life of man is then... death.
2. [end]. Wherefore, to adore nature, which in itself is dead, is to adore the fire which is in the sun of the world; they who do this are dead... They are called dead men who are in Hell.
Then, if he dies, he dies in the Lord.
Then they do not fear death, because if they die, they die in the Lord, and come into Heaven.
(How death is made to appear as a continuation of life.)
They exclaim, Thank God, we live, death has not extirpated us.
